title: Crash in the new helper inputs, fixed
text: Off turn the next hand is the current hand, which can hold more than 5 cards (after the opponent's Council Room); the C tables were sized for 5 cards and the workers died with 'stack smashing detected', which hung the pools (with three runs at once and the swap full this first looked like memory). Fixed, regression-tested, stress-tested on 3,000 games; z1h and z2 resumed from their checkpoints. z1 stays stopped at iteration 1,096 (flat at ~36% against rl-v1 for 400 iterations): its history is z1h's baseline.

title: Helper inputs: what the next hand brings, and what a card would change
text: 115 new inputs computed exactly from what the player knows (the draw pile's contents, then the reshuffle): the next hand's expected coins, chances of $3/$5/$6/$8, expected action cards, +Actions, +Buys, +Cards, expected VP gain (best Victory card it can afford) and VP after it; the deck's coins/actions/+Actions/+Buys/+Cards per 5 cards; and for every card, how one more copy changes coins, +Actions and +Buys per 5 cards. Added to z1 at iteration 1095 with zero weights (same play, checked on 20 games) as run z1h; z1 goes on unchanged as the comparison.
rejected: Learning these from the raw counts (the net has the counts but must learn division and hypergeometric odds); Monte Carlo estimates (noisy, and hard to reproduce bit-exactly in the browser).

title: Kingdom curriculum on z1: small edge, same style
text: Forked z1 at iteration 901 with 30% of training games on kingdoms without Witch, Militia, Bandit, Bureaucrat and Gardens. Goal checks at 925/950/975: vs GA 0.707/0.707/0.715 (z1 0.695/0.683/0.707), vs rl-v1 0.371/0.365/0.370 (z1 0.359/0.363/0.360): about +1 point each time, within noise, and the same style (0.56 vs 0.53 actions per turn). Stopped.

title: z2: a second run from zero, exploring from the start
text: z1's style locked in by iteration ~250 and nothing applied later (learning rate, entropy, kingdom curriculum) changed it. z2 starts from random weights again with an entropy bonus of 0.05 falling to 0.01 over 600 iterations (z1: 0.01 throughout; its entropy fell from 1.37 to 0.3 in 40 iterations) and the kingdom curriculum (30% of games without the attack and Gardens cards) from iteration 1. Same stages, same evaluation.
rejected: Only waiting for z1 to drift (rl-v1 needed ~2,000 league iterations); restarting z1 itself (it is the baseline).

title: Entropy bonus 0.04: no change of style
text: Forked z1 at iteration 801 with ent 0.04 (was 0.01): entropy rose 0.14 -> 0.20, but at iteration 850 the goal check was the same (vs GA 0.708 vs 0.710, vs rl-v1 0.340 vs 0.354) and so was the style (0.54 vs 0.52 actions per turn). Stopped. rl-v1's own history shows PPO can move from money to engines (0.49 -> 1.61 actions per turn over its 2,200 league iterations), slowly.

title: Learning rate 1e-3: no gain
text: Forked z1 at iteration 726 with lr 1e-3 (was 3e-4): KL rose from 0.002 to 0.006 and entropy from 0.15 to 0.18, but over 30 iterations the evaluation against the GA base was 0.692 vs z1's 0.704 and the training score against rl-v1 0.433 vs 0.448. Not worth the risk; stopped.

title: Checked: +Actions, +Cards and +Buys work
text: New tests (tests/test_vanilla.py): every card's +Cards/+Actions/+Buys/+$ is right in the engine, and in C-engine games through the network's decision interface a player is asked again after a Village or a Market, never beyond what the bonuses allow. The trained net uses a second buy as often as the GA genome (76% vs 72% of the turns it played a +Buy card), but it rarely chains actions: 0.51 actions per turn and 6% of turns with 2+ actions, against rl-v1's 1.61 and 28%. Self-play from zero found money + attacks (Witch, Militia, Gardens) and not engines (experiments/turn_usage.py).

title: Start from random weights, no imitation
text: rl-v2 tests whether the GA genome is a head start or a ceiling: same network, inputs and PPO as rl-v1, only the start changes. Self-play first, then the bots, then every earlier model.
rejected: Imitation first (that is rl-v1); a new architecture (would mix two changes into one comparison).

title: Stage 1 ends on a plateau, not a score
text: The first start ended self-play after 12 iterations, when it beat the bots 50% of the time. Self-play is the point of the project, so stage 1 now runs until the score against the GA genome has not improved for 60 iterations (at most 400): it shows how far self-play gets alone.
rejected: A fixed bots threshold (ended the stage after 3 minutes); a fixed iteration count (could stop while it is still learning, or waste hours on a plateau).

title: 1,500 games per iteration
text: Random players make long games with ~210 decisions each; 3,000 of them (rl-v1's setting) ran the 8 GB laptop out of memory. 1,500 fit with room for the evaluation.
rejected: Keeping 3,000 with float16 features (a change to the shared code that rl-v1 does not have).

title: Same evaluation games as rl-v1
text: The per-iteration evaluation and the goal checks use rl-v1's and az-v1's seeds, so every number compares directly with them. A new confirmation seed is kept for the end.
